SIP\xe2\x80\x99s (Subject Interface Package) and Authenticode \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 \xe2\x98 Eduardo NavarroJuly 11, 20081 Share 0 0 This is my first post so I'll make it short and sweet. What are SIPs? They are basically implementations of Subject Interface Packages, which allow the CryptAPI to interact with specific parts of the files in order to put, get, calculate and verify digital signatures on files.\xc2 In other words, this is how Windows handles Authenticode digital signatures from and to files. They tell the CryptAPI how to hash the file and where to put the signatures. Where can I find them? There are some\xc2 included as part of the\xc2 OS (at least on Vista). Locate in the %WINDIR%\\System32 directory. They usually have a naming ending with sip.dll, i.e. msisip.dll is the Microsoft Installer (.msi)\xc2 SIP. How can I use\xc2 them? They need to be\xc2 registered (regsvr32 <dll>)\xc2 in order to be usable/reachable to digital signature tools, such as SignTool. Signtool will automatically recognize it and be able to use it for different file formats. Any tips? Look for MSDN online since\xc2 installing MSDN locally will not have all available functions documented.
